transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Well, I came in because... I know this is probably going to sound really hard to explain, and honestly, if I were just listening to myself from the outside, I might wonder about it too, but a lot has been happening lately. I'm currently working as an operations manager, which is already a lot to juggle, but I'm also in the middle of my MBA program, so my schedule is just packed. But the main reason I made this appointment is that over the last few weeks—or maybe it's been a month, it's honestly a little hard to track with how fast the semester moves—I’ve become completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor we've been working with are quietly coordinating these massive career opportunities for me. 

And I don't mean they're just networking or offering to write a recommendation letter, it's much more intricate than that. It's like they are sending me these highly specific, coded signals about exactly where my career is supposed to go next. For example, the other day in our strategy seminar, my classmate made this very specific comment about scaling operations, and he used the exact phrasing I had written in a private notebook the night before. And then, maybe twenty minutes later, the startup advisor sent a message in our group Slack channel about "the right doors opening at the exact right time." If you look at the timestamps and the specific vocabulary they use, it’s all perfectly connected. It’s like this elaborate puzzle they’ve set up just for me to decode so I can take the right path, and I spend hours analyzing these little hints they keep dropping in class and online... it's just really overwhelming trying to keep up with all the signs they're sending me.
Do you think these signals are meant for you specifically, or could they be coincidences or messages meant for someone else?

Oh, no, I... I really don't think they could be for anyone else. I mean, I've tried to tell myself that, you know? Like, maybe it's just a coincidence, maybe I'm reading way too much into normal networking behavior. But it's just too specific to my life. Like I was saying, I am completely convinced that this classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating these massive opportunities specifically for me. It can't be for anyone else because the coded signals are perfectly tailored to my exact career trajectory. 

Like, if it were meant for someone else in the MBA cohort, why would the Slack messages align perfectly with my specific background in operations management? And it’s not just a passing thought, I am entirely convinced that these certain comments in class or the way they phrase things online are coded signals specifically about where my career is supposed to go next. I actually spent hours the other evening just mapping out the timeline of when I spoke to the advisor versus when the classmate made that comment in the seminar, and the probability of it being a coincidence is just... it's basically zero. 

Because they know I'm an operations manager right now, right? So they use words like 'bottlenecks' and 'throughput' but they use them in this very deliberate, pointed way while looking right in my direction, or tagging me in threads that seem completely unrelated to my current projects but actually contain these hidden directives just for me. It's like this highly personalized roadmap that only I have the key to. So, no, it's definitely for me. It has to be. I just wish they would be direct about it, honestly, because trying to decipher every single word they say to make sure I don't miss my chance is taking up so much of my mental energy, and I already have so much on my plate with work and school...

Have you ever felt like you're seeing these coded signals in things other than what your classmate and the startup advisor say or do, such as in TV shows, movies, or even random conversations with strangers?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I watch TV, of course, when I have the time, which honestly isn't that often lately because between the MBA coursework and my actual job, my evenings are pretty much spoken for. But when I do watch something, like if I put on a show just to have some background noise while I'm reviewing supply chain case studies, it's just a show. The characters are just saying their lines. I don't feel like the writers or the actors are trying to send me a message about my career or anything. 

And with strangers... no, not really. Like, if I'm at the coffee shop near campus and the barista asks how my day is going, or if I overhear someone on the bus talking about their weekend, it just sounds like normal conversation. It doesn't have that same... weight to it, you know? It doesn't feel like there's a hidden layer. 

It's really just the classmate and the advisor. That's what makes it so undeniable to me. If I were seeing signs everywhere, in every commercial or every random chat at the grocery store, I would probably think, 'Okay, I'm just incredibly stressed and my brain is making connections that aren't there.' Because I know stress can do weird things to you, and I am definitely under a massive amount of pressure right now. But because it's so localized, so specific to these two individuals who actually have the power and the network to influence my professional trajectory, it feels entirely different. It's confined to this very specific professional sphere. So, no, it's not the TV or random people on the street. It's just them, and it's just about my career.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretation of these signals might be incorrect?

I mean... yes and no? Like I was saying earlier, I know exactly how this sounds. I really do. I’m a very logical person, you know? I work as an operations manager, so my entire day-to-day job is about finding efficiencies, relying on hard data, and looking at concrete metrics, not just making wild guesses about things. So, of course, there are moments where I sit back and think, 'Okay, am I just misinterpreting this? Is the stress of the MBA and my job just getting to me?' 

I actually spent almost an entire weekend recently trying to convince myself that I was just overthinking it all. I pulled up the group Slack channels—because we use Slack for literally everything in this program, from group projects to the startup incubator updates—and I tried to look at their messages completely objectively. I tried to tell myself, 'Maybe he just meant scaling operations in a general sense,' or 'Maybe the advisor is just giving generic motivational advice when he talks about doors opening.' I really, really tried to poke holes in my own theory. I even started a spreadsheet—because that’s just how my brain works, I organize things—trying to map out alternative, totally mundane explanations for why they would use those exact phrases on those exact days. 

But every time I try to tell myself my interpretation is incorrect, I just... I can't. Because the evidence is just too overwhelming. Like I told you, I have just become completely convinced that this classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. It’s not just a gut feeling, it’s the actual pattern of it. The specific comments in class, the exact wording they choose in those Slack messages... they really are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

If it were just one comment, sure, I could write it off as a misunderstanding or a coincidence. But it’s the sheer volume of it. It’s the way the advisor will post a seemingly random article about supply chain logistics right after my classmate asks me a hyper-specific question about my current role at work during a seminar break. The timing is just too perfect, the vocabulary is too precise. So, yes, I’ve tried to consider that I’m wrong, because honestly? It would be so much easier if I were wrong. It would be so much less exhausting than trying to decode every single interaction while also managing my regular workload and studying for my midterms. But when I lay all the pieces out and look at them together, the logic holds up. I just know I'm right about what they're doing.
Do you think the classmate and the startup advisor are aware that you have figured out their coded signals?

I mean, yes, I really do think they're starting to catch on that I know. Actually, that kind of ties into the whole reason I even sought help and came in here to talk to someone. I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain to anyone on the outside, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me, like certain comments in class or Slack messages are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. And because I'm so hyper-aware of it now, I think my reactions are starting to give me away. 

Like, when they drop those specific signals, I can't help but react to let them know I'm picking up what they're putting down. Just last Thursday, for example, the advisor posted this article in the main incubator Slack channel about, um, supply chain restructuring, right? And he tagged my classmate, but not me. But the wording he used in the comment was verbatim a phrase I used in my operations management midterm. So I liked the message. Just a simple thumbs-up emoji on Slack, nothing crazy, just to show I saw it. 

But then, in the seminar the very next morning, my classmate sat two rows ahead of me, and right before the professor started speaking, he turned around, looked right at me, and just nodded. Just a single, very deliberate nod. It wasn't a casual 'good morning' nod, you know? It was an acknowledgment. It was him saying, 'We saw your thumbs up, we know you're following the plan.' 

So I really think they know that I’ve cracked the code. They know I understand that these aren't just random interactions. It’s almost like this unspoken dance we’re doing now, where they send the signal, I show them I’ve received it, and then they escalate it to the next level. It's just... it's incredibly intense to navigate, honestly. Trying to keep up this totally normal, professional facade while we're all secretly communicating on this entirely different wavelength takes so much focus. I mean, I have to constantly monitor my own expressions in class so I don't give away too much too soon, but I also have to make sure I give them enough feedback so they don't think I'm missing the opportunities they're setting up. It's like playing three-dimensional chess every single day.
Have you experienced feeling like other people or things, outside of your classmate and the startup advisor, are sending you hidden messages or signs about your life or career?

I know we kind of just touched on this, but no, really, it’s not anyone else. Like I was saying a few minutes ago, I don't walk down the street and think the billboards are talking to me, or that the news anchor on TV is giving me career advice. It’s strictly them. And honestly, that’s exactly why I came in here to see you today. I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain to anyone who isn't living it, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. 

It's just them. Nobody else. It's like certain comments they make in class or specific Slack messages they post are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. If it were happening with my boss at my day job, or my family, or just random people, I would probably think I was just severely sleep-deprived from trying to balance a full-time job as an operations manager with a master's degree. Because, believe me, the sleep deprivation is real. I’m running on maybe four hours of sleep most nights right now because I’m trying to keep up with the coursework, the reading, the actual job where I have real people relying on me to manage the supply chain... 

But because this is so incredibly localized, so specific to just this one classmate and this one advisor, it validates it for me. It’s a closed loop. My brain is trained to look for operational inefficiencies and patterns, right? That’s what I do for a living. I look at data and I find the connections. And all the data points directly to them, and only them, orchestrating this massive shift for my professional future. If my boss says we need to "optimize," she just means we need to cut shipping costs. But when the advisor says it in the Slack channel, it means something entirely different for my future. So, no, I definitely don't feel like other people or random things are sending me messages. It would be entirely illogical for anyone outside of that specific incubator network to have any bearing on my career trajectory anyway, so my mind wouldn't even go there. It's just the two of them.
Have you ever had thoughts like this about other people or situations before, outside of your current MBA program?

No, honestly? Never. I’ve never experienced anything even remotely like this before. Like I said, I’m an operations manager, so my whole life before this was just very straightforward, very face-value. A equals B, you know? But before this current stretch... this whole period of just being so incredibly energized and driven... I never had messages feel coded like this. Never. 

And it's funny you ask about other situations, because it’s not just the Slack messages or the classroom stuff that’s new. There are other things, too, that I haven't really mentioned yet, like... sometimes, recently, I'll be sitting at my desk at work, or pulling a late night studying for a finance exam, and I will hear my name. Just my name, spoken out loud, clear as day, when there is absolutely no one else in the room. And I'll look around, and obviously the office is totally empty or my apartment is empty, but I know I heard it. That kind of thing—hearing my name when no one is there, or feeling like normal conversations have these hidden, coded layers meant just for me—none of that ever happened to me in the past. It’s all very new. 

Really, all of these experiences only started once my mood and my workload intensity completely shifted. It was right after I began the MBA prerequisites. I remember I took on this massive course load on top of my full-time job, and I fully expected to be exhausted, but instead of crashing, I just... I got this huge surge of energy, this intense drive that I've never really felt before. I was just going and going, and my mind was moving so fast, making all these brilliant connections that I wouldn't have seen otherwise. So, yeah, to answer your question, it is entirely tied to this specific time in my life. Before the MBA prerequisites and this huge shift in my energy and my workload, I never interpreted things this way or heard things like my name being called out of nowhere. It’s strictly a recent development.
Do you feel like your thoughts are well-organized and helping you achieve your goals, or are they disjointed and hard to follow?

You know, it’s… it’s really a double-edged sword, if I’m being completely honest. Because on one hand, I feel like I’m having these massive, groundbreaking realizations, but on the other hand… well, to answer your question about them being organized or disjointed, they are just moving so incredibly fast right now. Like, warp speed. 

My mind has just been jumping constantly. One second I’m thinking about market expansion strategies for the incubator project, and then before I can even finish that thought, my brain pivots entirely to my MBA coursework, and then suddenly I’m analyzing the org charts at my day job and figuring out how they need to be completely restructured, and then, out of nowhere, I’m planning out the logistics of moving abroad because I just know that’s where the advisor is ultimately trying to steer my career. It’s all happening so quickly that I can barely keep up with my own brain. 

I’ll literally be sitting at my laptop, right? And I’ll have this brilliant flash of insight, so I’ll open a new document to type it out. But before the program even finishes loading, I’ve already had three other completely different, equally important ideas, so I open another document, and another one, and suddenly I have like five blank documents open on my screen. And I’ll just sit there staring at the blinking cursor, and I will completely forget which idea I was actually trying to capture in the first place. 

It’s incredibly frustrating because I know the thoughts are valuable, and I know they're all leading somewhere important, they’re just… they’re firing off like a million fireworks all at once. Trying to organize them into something coherent is taking so much effort right now. I mean, I’m an operations manager, I organize chaotic systems for a living, so to have my own thoughts outpace my ability to file them properly is just wild to experience. I just have so much going on up there, and it won't slow down enough for me to get it all on paper.
Are these rapid thoughts and ideas interfering with your ability to complete tasks at work or in your MBA program?

Yeah, that’s exactly it. That’s really the core of the issue right now, and honestly, it's the main reason I finally decided to come in. I mean, I’m still showing up, right? I haven’t missed a single day of work, I log in right on time, I haven’t skipped a single MBA lecture. I am physically present and I'm putting in the hours. But... the actual execution of my day-to-day tasks is where everything is just starting to unravel, and it is incredibly frustrating for me because I'm usually the one holding the entire system together. 

Just last week, my manager—who normally trusts me completely, we’ve always had a fantastic working relationship—she actually started formally documenting my mistakes. It was this whole situation with missed handoffs on the regional distribution schedule. I was sitting at my desk, so caught up in redesigning our entire logistics network in my head because of all these rapid-fire ideas, that I completely forgot to send the finalized routing slips to the warehouse team. And then the next day, I didn't follow through on the vendor confirmation calls because my brain was already ten steps ahead on something else. So she pulled me into her office and literally showed me this written list of my "unreliable follow-throughs." Which is just... it’s so completely unlike me. I’m an operations manager! Reliability and follow-through are literally my entire job description. 

And it’s not just bleeding into my job, it’s happening in the MBA program, too. We had this huge group assignment for my strategic management class, and I naturally took the lead because I had all these incredible, complex connections firing in my brain about how to structure the case study. But when we submitted our preliminary draft, the professor actually pulled me aside and directly questioned my judgment. He told me my contributions were completely off-base and that I was derailing the group’s focus. He actually asked if I was taking the assignment seriously! Which... I mean, I was taking it more seriously than anyone else in that group! I was seeing all these strategic layers they couldn't even fathom! 

But because they can't see what I'm seeing, it just looks to them like I'm dropping the ball or making terrible decisions. The strain it’s putting on my relationships with my coworkers, my manager, my project group... it’s getting really, really intense. The tension is just palpable everywhere I go now. Like I said, I'm still showing up to everything, but the friction at work and at school is getting so bad, and the professional relationships I've worked so hard to build are getting so strained, that I finally just realized I couldn't manage it entirely on my own anymore. I realized I needed help. I can’t keep operating with my brain moving at warp speed if it’s going to cost me my career and my master's degree.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain your relationships with friends and family due to your current thoughts and preoccupations?

Well, yes, honestly, it really is spilling over into my personal life, especially with my boyfriend. Which is strange, because... well, most days lately, I have actually felt unusually switched on. Like, incredibly optimistic. I wake up and I just have this overwhelming sense that I’m right on the edge of something huge, you know? Like my whole life is building to this massive crescendo and I'm finally unlocking my true potential. And you would think that feeling so positive and so driven would make me a joy to be around, but... it’s actually doing the exact opposite. 

Because my brain is moving at that warp speed I was talking about, I expect everyone else to be right there with me. And when they aren't, I just... I have zero patience. None. I find myself snapping at people over the most ridiculous, minor things. Like, I’ll snap at my project teammates if they take more than ten minutes to reply to a Slack message, or... or with my boyfriend. We live together, and usually, I am the most patient person in the world with him. But just the other morning, he was taking maybe two extra minutes to pour his coffee before we left the apartment, and I just completely lost it on him. Over coffee! A two-minute delay that normally wouldn’t bother me at all, and I was practically yelling at him about how he's holding me back and wasting my time when I have these huge things to accomplish. 

And I can see it in his face, you know? He just looks at me like he doesn't even recognize who he's talking to, because I’m bouncing around the apartment talking about how amazing everything is and how we're on the brink of greatness, and then in the next breath I'm biting his head off because he paused to tie his shoe. It’s just... if there is even the slightest delay in my day, I get so intensely irritable. So, yeah, it’s definitely making things really difficult at home, because he feels like he has to walk on eggshells around me, even though I keep telling him I’ve never felt better or more optimistic in my entire life. It’s a very weird contradiction to live with, feeling so incredibly good but being so quick to anger over absolutely nothing.
Are you finding it challenging to enjoy or participate in activities you used to like outside of work and school due to your current preoccupations?

Honestly? No, not at all. I mean, if anything, it’s the exact opposite. I am enjoying things so much more intensely right now, it’s just that the actual *types* of things I want to spend my time on have shifted completely. 

Like, okay, before all this started, my boyfriend and I would have these very standard, predictable weekends. We’d go to the farmer's market, maybe I'd do a little yoga, we'd watch a movie on the couch, maybe do some meal prep for the week... very typical, right? But now? I literally don't have the time or the patience for that kind of mundane stuff because I am just so incredibly energized. So, it's not that I *can't* enjoy my old hobbies, it's just that they feel so... small? So incredibly small and slow compared to what my brain is focused on right now. 

Just last Saturday, instead of our usual routine, I woke up at 4 AM—wide awake, completely refreshed—and I decided I needed to learn everything there is to know about emerging tech markets in Southeast Asia. I spent eight hours straight just absorbing data, building these massive, beautiful spreadsheets, mapping out potential investment strategies. And I loved every single second of it! It was exhilarating! 

So, if you're asking if I'm sitting around feeling down or unable to enjoy life, absolutely not. I have never felt more alive or more capable of enjoying my time. I’m just choosing to spend that time on things that actually matter, things that are going to propel me forward, rather than just, you know, watching Netflix or doing a puzzle. My old activities just can't compete with the rush of what I'm working on now, so I just don't bother with them. But I definitely wouldn't say I've lost my ability to have fun or enjoy myself. It's just a different kind of fun now.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Sleep? Um, no, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I know I just told you about that 4 AM thing last Saturday, which I realize probably sounds like I'm not sleeping, but that was really just a one-off because I was so incredibly fired up about that tech market research. But as a general rule? No, I haven't noticed that I need less sleep overall. 

I'm actually incredibly meticulous about my sleep schedule. You know, being an operations manager, you learn pretty quickly that the whole supply chain falls apart if the central hub—which is me—isn't properly maintained. So I have this very strict nighttime routine that I stick to. I start winding down at exactly 10:30, I do this whole multi-step skincare regimen that takes exactly eighteen minutes, and I make absolutely sure I am in bed by 11:00 PM. I even wear a smart ring that logs my REM cycles, my heart rate variability, and my deep sleep percentages, and I analyze the data every single morning. Honestly, my total sleep duration hasn't really changed at all. I'm still getting my standard seven hours most nights. 

It's just that when I *am* awake, my brain is operating at, like, 200% capacity. But I definitely still feel like I need that baseline rest to keep the whole system running smoothly. If I actually tried to survive on two or three hours a night, I'm pretty sure I'd feel completely exhausted just like anyone else would. So, yeah, despite how fast and intense everything is moving during the day, my actual need for sleep hasn't dropped off. I'm just squeezing way, way more productivity and life into my waking hours than I ever used to.
Have you found that you can function normally with less sleep than you used to?

Well, no, like I... I think I just touched on this, but no, definitely not. I haven't found that at all. If anything, I'm hyper-aware of the fact that I *can't* function normally if I cut corners on my sleep. 

Like I was saying with my smart ring and my whole schedule, I still absolutely require my standard seven hours to operate at this level. I mean, think about it like a high-performance sports car, right? You can't just put cheap gas in it or skip the maintenance and expect it to run at top speed without the engine blowing out. And right now, my brain is basically a Ferrari. It is running so beautifully, so incredibly fast, but it needs that premium fuel, which is my sleep. 

If I tried to just sleep three or four hours, I wouldn't be functioning normally at all—I'd be totally exhausted, probably getting brain fog, and I wouldn't be able to execute all these massive plans I'm putting together. I'd be dragging myself through the day just like anyone else would. So, no, I'm not one of those people who suddenly doesn't need to sleep to get by. I just make sure that when I am awake, every single second is maximized and I'm operating at absolute peak efficiency. But the sleep itself? No, that hasn't decreased, and I definitely couldn't function at this level if it did.
Are you feeling like your current thoughts and behaviors are significantly impacting your daily functioning or causing you a lot of distress?

Well, distress? No, I wouldn't say distress, because like I said, I feel incredible, I feel like a Ferrari. But... okay, I will admit that things are getting a little... complicated, I guess you could say, in terms of my daily functioning. Which is actually why I'm here. 

See, the problem isn't that my ideas aren't brilliant—they are, they absolutely are—but the people around me just cannot keep up with the pace I'm setting right now. For example, at work, my manager—who is usually very supportive, we usually have a great dynamic—she recently pulled me aside and told me she’s started formally documenting some things. She claims there have been "missed handoffs" and that my "follow-through has been unreliable." Which, to be fair, maybe I did skip a few minor procedural steps on the last quarterly report, but only because I was completely restructuring our entire vendor communication protocol! I was fixing the bigger picture, but she’s hyper-focused on these tiny, administrative details that honestly don't matter in the grand scheme of what I'm building. But still, the fact that she’s documenting it... that’s a red flag for my career trajectory, you know? 

And it's not just work. I'm also taking a few graduate classes right now, and last week, my professor actually pulled me aside after class. We had this huge group assignment, and I essentially took over the whole thing because my group members were moving at a glacial pace. I completely pivoted our project focus to something way more innovative, and my professor actually questioned my judgment. He said I was completely off-syllabus and that I wasn't collaborating. 

So, I'm still showing up to everything. I'm at work every day, I'm at all my classes, I'm not hiding in bed or anything like that. But... yeah, the relationships with my boss and my professors are definitely getting pretty strained. People are getting frustrated with me, and I'm getting frustrated with them for not seeing the vision. It's causing enough friction that I finally thought, okay, maybe I need to talk to someone and figure out how to navigate this, because I can't afford to have my career or my grades derailed just because other people can't operate at my current frequency.
Do you feel like you can stop thinking about these coded signals and career opportunities when you want to?

Stop thinking about them? Um... I mean, it’s not really a matter of just turning it off, because why would I want to ignore something so massive? And honestly, this is actually a big part of why I came in to talk to someone, because I know this sounds really, really hard to explain to anyone who isn't seeing the whole board. But I’ve been completely, one hundred percent convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this prominent startup advisor are quietly coordinating all these incredible opportunities for me behind the scenes. 

So when you ask if I can just stop thinking about it, it's like... how can I? It's happening right in front of me! Like, I'll be sitting in my evening seminar, and this classmate will make certain comments in class—very specific phrasing about market disruption or leadership vacuums—and I know, I just know, that it's a coded signal meant specifically for me about where my career is supposed to go next. And then I'll get Slack messages in our cohort channel, and the way they are worded, or the exact timing of when the advisor chimes in, it’s all connected. It's this brilliant, intricate web. 

I’ll try to just sit down and do my regular operations management work, or, you know, do my skincare routine like I told you about, but my brain just keeps looping back to decode what the latest Slack message really meant. I’ll spend hours analyzing the subtext because I don't want to miss the opportunity they are setting up for me. It’s like they are testing me to see if I’m sharp enough to catch the hints and step into this new role they're preparing me for. So, no, I can't really just switch it off, because it feels way too important, and honestly, it takes up a huge amount of my mental bandwidth trying to piece every single little clue together every single day.
Can you choose to think about something else when you start analyzing these coded signals?

Well, like I was just saying a second ago, it's really not a choice. I can't just... pivot my attention. I mean, I try! Sometimes I'll say to myself, 'Okay, let's just focus on making dinner, let's just chop these vegetables and listen to a podcast,' but then my mind is immediately right back on it. 

Because, like I brought up—and I know it sounds so hard to explain to someone who isn't in the room experiencing it—I have been completely, absolutely convinced that this MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these huge opportunities for me. It's happening in real time. So if I try to think about something else, I just feel this intense, magnetic pull back to those certain comments they made in class. I'll literally put the knife down and pull my phone back out while I'm cooking just to re-read those Slack messages for the fifth time. 

I have to know what the coded signals mean for where my career is supposed to go. I can't just choose to ignore a roadmap that's being laid out specifically for me, you know? If someone is handing you the keys to your entire future, you don't just look away to think about mundane things. It demands my attention, every single time, so choosing to focus on something else just really isn't an option.
Can you control when you start thinking about these coded signals?

Control when I start? I feel like we're going in circles a bit here, doctor, because like I literally just tried to explain... it's not a faucet I can just turn on and off. I came in today specifically because of this exact issue. I know it sounds so incredibly hard to explain to anyone who isn't living it, but I have been completely, one hundred percent convinced that this specific MBA classmate of mine and that startup advisor are quietly, behind the scenes, coordinating these massive opportunities for me. 

So when you ask about controlling when I *start* thinking about it... the thoughts start because the signals are actively happening all around me! It's not like I wake up and schedule in, you know, 'from 2 PM to 3 PM I will think about my future.' No, if I log into Slack for a totally unrelated reason, just to check a project deadline or see if a vendor replied, boom, there's a message. And it's not just a normal message, it's a coded signal about where my career is supposed to go. 

Or I'll be sitting in class, not even thinking about my career trajectory at all, just taking notes on supply chain logistics, and then my classmate will make a certain comment. And the very moment that comment hits my ears, the analysis starts. I don't sit there and think, 'Hmm, should I start decoding this now?' My brain just immediately recognizes the pattern. It's like... if someone throws a ball at your face, you don't consciously decide to blink, you just blink! So the second I see or hear one of these hints they're dropping for me, the gears are turning. I can't control the start of it any more than I can control them sending the signals in the first place, which, again, is exactly why I felt I needed to talk to a professional, because it's just so all-consuming when everything around you is a sign you have to read.
Do you feel like you can stop thinking about these coded signals even when you want to focus on other things?
